title: Performance Table Reader
description: Numeric challenge sequence on the Twin City Fan RBA 913 performance table excerpt (Catalog 902, page 24): for six duty points the learner types RPM and BHP by direct reading or linear interpolation and picks the fan class; each answer is marked, then a class overlay shows the shading.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Reading and interpolating a catalog performance table
learningObjectives: The learner will use an excerpt of the RBA 913 performance table to find the RPM and BHP for a duty point, by direct reading or linear interpolation within ±1%, and to name the fan class the point requires.

accessibility.notes: describe() text (fallback mode); duty points, verdicts, cell values under the keyboard cursor and the summary are announced through FP.announce (aria-live); RPM, BHP and class each get a ✓/✗ mark; the class overlay uses shading plus bold (Class 32) or italic (Class 45) as in the catalog; feedback pairs ✓/✗ with solid/dashed borders; Enter checks and advances, arrow keys and S move and pin a grid cursor.

controls.label: RPM
controls.purpose: Your fan speed for the duty point

controls.label: BHP
controls.purpose: Your brake horsepower for the duty point

controls.label: Class 22 / Class 32 / Class 45
controls.purpose: The class the duty point requires

controls.label: Check
controls.purpose: Mark RPM, BHP and class, then turn the class overlay on (Enter)

controls.label: Next duty point
controls.purpose: Load the next point and turn the overlay off; after point 6, Show summary (Enter)

controls.label: Class overlay
controls.purpose: Show or hide class shading; available after Check and after the summary

controls.label: Scratch panel
controls.purpose: Pin bracketing cells and type your fraction f (not scored, never computes the answer)

controls.label: Start over
controls.purpose: Back to duty point 1 with the score cleared

rules: Double interpolation interpolates airflow within each bracketing pressure column first, then pressure between the two results
Direct readings must match exactly (±1 RPM, ±0.01 BHP); interpolated answers within ±1%
A duty point is correct only when RPM, BHP and class are all correct
Two attempts per point, first scored; mastery is 5 of 6
assumptions: Standard air; installation type B and D; BHP excludes transmission losses and appurtenance effects, as the catalog footer states
limitations: Excerpt only (3,348-4,836 CFM, 4-32 in. SP); straight-line interpolation is an approximation, confirm in Fan Selector before quoting

sources: Twin City Fan Catalog 902, RB Industrial Fans (November 2017), page 24, RBA 913

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Compute RPM and BHP and commit a class before feedback; the class overlay is revealed only after Check
keyQuestions: What speed and power does this duty need, and which class must you order?
Which two cells bracket this duty point?
commonMisconceptions: The class is decided by the static pressure column alone.
Interpolation can use the nearest cell instead of the two bracketing cells.
A duty point between two pressure columns can be interpolated in one step.
assessmentOpportunities: Score 'Duty points correct: n of 6' (first attempts); mastery is 5 of 6; the summary lists points not right on the first attempt with their answers.
